hero.title: UG Electrical Engineering in France
hero.subtitle: \\Undergraduate electrical engineering in France\\ is a promising option for students interested in \\electrical power systems, electronics, automation, renewable energy, telecommunications, and industrial technology\.

overview: In France, engineering schools are associated with sectors such as energy, transportation, manufacturing, electronics, telecommunications and industrial automation.
\\Technical education\\: Study \\electrical circuits, electrical machines, power systems, electronics, and control systems.
\\Learning related to the industry:\\ Depending on the program, students may take part in practical laboratory sessions, design projects and work placements.

universities.desc: IUT 1 : \\Université Grenoble Alpes\\ provides a three:year \\BUT ( University Bachelor of Technology ) in Electrical Engineering and Industrial Computing\\ (\Génie électrique et informatique industrielle\, GEII). ### Students can choose to specialize in \\electricity and energy management, automation and industrial computing or electronics and embedded systems\. The program is taught in French. ### Licence EEA : This route gives a broader academic foundation in \\electronics, electrical energy and automation\\ and can prepare students for further education at master's level. It is taught in French. ### 4. Eligibility for Undergraduate Electrical Engineering in France The \\entry requirements for electrical engineering in France\\ normally include: Completion of secondary studies equivalent to the French baccalauréat. A strong academic background in \\mathematics and physics\. Chemistry or other science subjects as needed. \\Knowledge of the French language\\ for courses taught in French or \\knowledge of the English language\\ for courses taught in English. Any entrance test, interview or further assessment that may be required. Class 12 with maths and physics is typically relevant for \\Indian students\. The combination of subjects and minimum marks differ from institution to institution. \\English taught electrical engineering courses\\ Students may need to apply for \\IELTS, TOEFL or another accepted English qualification\. sections.title: Why Study Electrical Engineering in France?
sections.lead: In France, engineering schools are associated with sectors such as energy, transportation, manufacturing, electronics, telecommunications and industrial automation.

groups.text: Some of the main benefits are:

items: \\Technical education\\: Study \\electrical circuits, electrical machines, power systems, electronics, and control systems.
\\Learning related to the industry:\\ Depending on the program, students may take part in practical laboratory sessions, design projects and work placements.
\\Specialisation choices:\\ Look into \\renewable energy, smart grids, industrial automation, embedded systems, and electric mobility\.
\\International study pathways:\\ Some \\bachelor's programs in France\\ are taught in English, but most traditional electrical engineering courses are in French.
\\Further study:\\ Graduates can apply for relevant \\master's programmes\\ or engineering school pathways, after completion, subject to admission requirements.
\\Career flexibility:\\ \\Electrical engineering skills\\ are transferable to energy, manufacturing, transportation, building systems and technology industries

sections.title: Electrical Engineering Courses in France
sections.lead: \\Undergraduate electrical engineering programs in France\\ train students to design, operate, test and maintain electrical and electronic systems.

items: Popular fields of study are:
\\Electrical Engineering:\\ Electrical circuits, machines, power systems and electrical installations.
\\Electronics Engineering:\\ designing of circuits, electronic circuits, sensors and digital systems.
\\Electrical Power Engineering:\\ Generation, transmission, distribution and conversion of power and energy.
\\Renewable Energy Engineering:\\ Solar, wind, storage and integration with the electrical grid.
\\Automation and Control Engineering:\\ Industrial control systems, instrumentation, sensors and automated processes.
\\Embedded Systems:\\ Microcontrollers, electronics hardware, real-time systems, connected devices.
Signal processing, electronic communication systems, and communication networks are all included in telecommunications engineering.
\\Industrial Computing:\\ Control systems, programming, automation, and digital manufacturing.
Duration of program typically
Bachelor's degree or Licence\\ : often three years.
Traditional French engineering-school track:\\ usually 5 years after secondary school.

sections.title: Admission Requirements for French Undergraduate Studies in Electrical Engineering
sections.lead: \\Typical Admission requirements for electrical engineering in France\\ are:

items: Marksheet/academic transcript of Class 10 and Class 12.
Certificate of secondary school completion.
Valid Passport
Proof of \\competence in French or English\\ if necessary.
Motivation letter or statement of purpose.
CV (if required).
Letters of recommendation, if needed.
Application form completed.
Results of entrance examination or interview where applicable.
Selective engineering programs may consider \\academic performance, preparation in mathematics and physics, motivation and suitability for technical study\\

sections.title: Cost of Electrical Engineering in France
sections.lead: The cost of tuition fees in electrical engineering in France varies depending on the institution, the diploma, the student status and possible exemptions.

items: Public higher education tuition fees
For the \\academic year 2026-2027\\, the following differentiated registration fees are published by Campus France for non-EU students subject to the relevant national rules:
Bachelor's degree level \| €2,902 Master's level degree \| €3,950 \| \| PhD \| €398
The regular yearly rate for eligible students published in the French/EU category is €178 for a bachelor degree and €630 for many public engineering-degree programs.
Other Expenses of Living
Students should also plan for:
Housing and public utilities.
Supplies and food.
Local transport
Expenses related to insurance and health.
Books, equipment and personal costs.
Costs related to residence and visa.
The cost of living in France will depend on the city, the type of accommodation and your lifestyle.

sections.title: Admission Process of Undergraduate Electrical Engineering in France
sections.lead: Here is the common \\admission process for undergraduate electrical engineering in France\\:

items: 1. \\Select your specialty:\\ Pick from electrical power, electronics, automation, renewable energy or embedded systems.
2. \\Make a shortlist of universities:\\ Compare the curriculum, length of the course, language of teaching, accreditation and fees.
3. \\Check the application channel:\\ See if you should apply directly to the institution or via an official admissions platform or the \\Études en France procédure\.
4. \\Gather your documents:\\ Collect your academic transcripts, passport information, language test scores, and any required motivation letter.
5. \\Submit application:\\ Complete the application by the published deadline date.
6. \\Complete selection steps:\\ Complete any entrance test or interview required.
7. \\Accept the offer:\\ Follow the enrollment instructions provided by the institution.
8. \\Arrange your student visa:\\ Once you have received the required admission documents, proceed with the applicable \\French student visa procedure\\

sections.title: Accreditation and recognition of Electrical Engineering in France
sections.lead: Accreditation of electrical engineering in France helps students to know the qualification they will receive and how it relates to further study or employment.

items: The \\Commission des titres d'ingénieur (CTI)\\ assesses the quality of the French engineering programs entitled to award the \diplôme d'ingénieur\ and authorizes the establishments to award the title.
A separate qualification is the three-year bachelor's degree or \\ BUT qualification \.
Students are to:
Check the exact qualification mentioned.
Check \\CTI accreditation\\ if you are looking for a French engineering diploma specifically.
Possibility of pursuing a master's degree or engineering cycle.
See if there are any requirements for professional recognition in the country where you plan to work.

faqs.q: \\Q1. Can Indian students pursue undergraduate electrical engineering in France?
faqs.a: Yes. \\Indian students can study electrical engineering in France\\ by applying to eligible bachelor's, BUT, and engineering school programs if they meet the academic, language and application requirements.

faqs.q: How many years does an undergraduate electrical engineering degree take in France?
faqs.a: You usually study \\three years\\ for a \\bachelor's degree or BUT in electrical engineering. The classic \\French engineering-school route\\ typically takes five years of study following high school.

faqs.q: \\Q3. Are French electrical engineering courses taught in English?\\
faqs.a: Some programs are taught in English, such as \\INSA Lyon's bachelor's program on electrical engineering and electrical network infrastructure. Many traditional electrical engineering courses are taught in French, so check the language of instruction.

faqs.q: What is the cost of undergraduate electrical engineering in France?
faqs.a: fees depend on qualification and institution The published differentiated fee for bachelor level non-EU students under the rules of the relevant public institution for \\2026-2027\\ is €2,902 per year. There are some programs which have separate fee schedules or exceptions.
